newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-WMC eyes growth as profits rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-WMC eyes growth as profits rise.

text.p: Australian nickel, gold and alumina group WMC Ltd on Thursday announced a 20.4 percent leap in annual profit and vowed to continue aggressive expansion by developing resource projects worldwide.
"Our objective is to maximise shareholder value by finding, acquiring, developing and operating mineral resource projects throughout the world," managing director Hugh Morgan said.
WMC reported net equity profit of A$386.2 million for the year to June 30 and declared an 11 cent final dividend, up from 12 cents, making 22 cents for the year, up from 20 cents.
Morgan told reporters in Melbourne that the result had been achieved through higher nickel and copper sales and higher nickel and alumina prices.
Morgan predicted flat to higher output of WMC's key commodities in fiscal 1996/97 coupled with lower unit costs but would not make any prediction of the company's future profits.
WMC's capital expenditure budget for 1996/97 is about A$600 million, a similar level to 1994/95 but down on last year.
WMC's largest domestic growth commitment is the A$1.25 billion expansion of the Olympic Dam copper/gold/uranium/silver mine in South Australia.

"The momentum for that is now gathering pace. Real dollars won't be spent until early next year. Now it's a question of optimisation and the process of finalising the arrangements with plant contractors," Morgan noted.
Expansion of the mine will lower costs and see its annual copper and uranium oxide production more than double to 200,000 tonnes and 3,700 tonnes respectively by 2001.
Other domestic growth opportunies included the St Ives gold mine expansion and 50 percent spare capacity in its Goldfields gas transmission pipeline, both in Western Australia, Morgan said.
WMC has a range of offshore growth opportunities in Uzbekistan, the Philippines and Cuba.

Negotiations continue with the Uzbekistan government over the development of the Zarmitan gold deposit, which is estimated to hold 24 million tonnes of auriferous ore containing 10 grams of gold per tonne.
"As we speak the negotiations are continuing. We have the preferred tender (for the project) and we are ... hopefully resolving the outstanding issues," Morgan said.
Evaluative drilling of the promising Tampakan copper prospect on Mindanao island, the Philippines, was progressing he said.

In Cuba, evaluation of the Pinares de Mayari West nickel deposit in partnership with state-owned Commercial Caribbean Nickel SA had commenced with the negotiation of government approvals and contractual documentation expected to be completed by the end of 1996.
Morgan reaffirmed that the Cuban assets were unlikely to be affected by tough sanctions due to be imposed the United States against Cuba under the Helms-Burton Act.
"Our present advice is that we are not subject to that (act)," he said.
WMC also foresees expanded alumina production resulting from expanded refinery capacity at its 40 percent-owned global alumina joint venture with Aluminum Co of America, Morgan said
